slides.title: Similar Triangles; Indirect Measurement
slides.note: Post the learning target. Say one line and nothing else yet: “Today: triangles of the same shape and different sizes — and a tree measured by its shadow.”

slides.title: Warm-Up
slides.sub: On your own. Four minutes. No notes.
slides.note: Q3 is today's k: copy ÷ original, 4 ÷ 10 = 0.4 — a copy smaller than the original. Q4 is the same multiplying on a drawing. Two minutes silent, then reveal.

slides.title: Warm-Up
slides.note: Reveal. Ask for the band each question came from only if time allows.

slides.title: Vocabulary
slides.sub: The new words, before they are used.
slides.note: Read each word and its meaning once; the notes use them next. Students copy the words, not the definitions.

slides.title: Notes
slides.sub: Copy the rule and the example.
slides.note:
The state guide's pair: 6, 8, 10 and 9, 12, 15 (the second drawn turned over). Match shortest to shortest, middle to middle, longest to longest — or angle to angle — never by where a side sits on the page. 9 ÷ 6, 12 ÷ 8 and 15 ÷ 10 are all 1.5: similar. Equal angles, sides in one ratio; the same shape, not the same size.
OFF: 'Similar: one k on every side. Match by size, not by place.'

slides.title: Notes
slides.note:
The two triangles are similar, and the 4-side matches the 10-side (both shortest). k = copy ÷ original = 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5, and every other side is multiplied by it: 6 × 2.5 = 15, 7 × 2.5 = 17.5. A proportion (4/10 = 6/x) is the same thing written as fractions.
OFF: 'One matching pair gives k. Every side times k.'

slides.title: Notes
slides.note:
At the same moment the sun's rays come in at one angle, so a person and a tree with their shadows make two similar right triangles (the state guide's task). The tree's shadow is 20 ÷ 4 = 5 times the person's, so the tree is 5 × 6 = 30 ft. Is 30 ft a realistic tree? Yes.
OFF: 'Same sun, same angle: similar triangles.'

slides.title: Example 1
slides.note: Ask which side of the second triangle matches the 5 before anyone divides: the shortest, 15 — wherever it sits.

slides.title: Example 1
slides.note: Sorted: 5, 7, 9 and 15, x, y — the 5 and the 15 are both shortest. k = 15 ÷ 5 = 3; x = 7 × 3 = 21, y = 9 × 3 = 27. A board with 17 and 19 added 10 to every side.

slides.title: Your Turn
slides.sub: Same steps, your numbers. Boards up when done.
slides.note: k = 12 ÷ 3 = 4; 5 × 4 = 20, 7 × 4 = 28. A board with 14 and 16 added 9.

slides.title: Your Turn
slides.note: Reveal; name what a wrong board most likely did (see the note above).

slides.title: Example 2
slides.note: Ask why the two triangles are similar: the same sun at the same moment — one angle for both rays.

slides.title: Example 2
slides.note: Shadow to shadow: k = 15 ÷ 3 = 5, so the pole is 5 × 5 = 25 ft. A board with 9 set the ratio up crosswise (15 × 3 ÷ 5); one with 17 added 12.

slides.title: Your Turn
slides.sub: Same steps, your numbers. Boards up when done.
slides.note: k = 12 ÷ 1.5 = 8; 2 × 8 = 16 m. A board with 9 set it up crosswise.

slides.title: Your Turn
slides.note: Reveal; name what a wrong board most likely did (see the note above).

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 1 of 9
slides.note: Sorted, the pairs are 8 and 12, 12 and 18, 14 and 21: each ratio 1.5, so similar. A board that checked only two ratios has the right verdict by luck.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 1 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 2 of 9
slides.note: k = 18 ÷ 6 = 3; 24 cm and 33 cm. A board with 20 and 23 added 12 to every side.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 2 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 3 of 9
slides.note: The copy is smaller, so k is under 1: 5 ÷ 20 = 0.25. 12 × 0.25 = 3 and 16 × 0.25 = 4. A board with 48 and 64 divided the other way.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 3 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 4 of 9
slides.note: Diagnostic. Option A matched by position (the 8 sits where the 9 sat before the turn), option B matched the middle side to the longest, option D looked for an equal side. Split? Sixty seconds, convince your neighbour, re-vote.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 4 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 5 of 9
slides.note: Diagnostic. Option A added 2, option C passes two ratios and fails the third, option D kept two sides equal. Split? Sixty seconds, convince your neighbour, re-vote.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 5 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 6 of 9
slides.note: k = 15 ÷ 2.5 = 6, so the tree is 4 × 6 = 24 ft. A board with about 9.4 set the ratio up crosswise (15 × 2.5 ÷ 4).

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 6 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 7 of 9
slides.note: Both triangles start at A, so the big one's base is the whole 8 m: k = 8 ÷ 2 = 4, h = 2.4 m. A board with 1.8 used the 6 m between the uprights.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 7 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 8 of 9
slides.note: The extra-number board (ruling 22): the 45 years is bait. Ground to ground, k = 16 ÷ 4 = 4; the pole is 5 × 4 = 20 ft. The words say the triangles are similar, as every mirror item here does (the book's test mirror never says, audit D47).

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 8 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 9 of 9
slides.sub: Take your time. Boards up when you have written it.
slides.note: Written, and the exit evidence: adding the same amount is the state's 'similar means equal' error in another form.

slides.title: Whiteboards   ·   Question 9 of 9
slides.note: Reveal. Scan the back row first; question the blank boards before the wrong ones.

slides.title: Independent Set
slides.sub: Six questions. On your own, in writing.
slides.note: Hand out the Independent Set; the same six questions are on the board. Silent work. Circulate and mark what you see; do not teach. Whatever is not finished goes home.

slides.title: IXL
slides.note: IXL: every listed skill is required, SmartScore 67. Due at the start of the next class.
